EDIT: For clarification's sake, this is what I mean by steel. Maybe Americans call it something different. I am also aware that re-alignment steels are not the same thing as actual sharpening steels (or various sharpening devices).

Do practically all sharpening devices work on all knives, or are there hardness levels on sharpening devices as well?
Steel: Your steel needs to be harder than your knives. How do you know how hard your knives / steel are?

The graph thingy small squares are a code for the date the knives were made.

Include the word rockwell in an internet search on your knife, and it will likely turn up the hardness information you seek.

For example, a search for "Henckel 30047-180 Rockwell" showed that knife has a 57° Rockwell Hardness. I imagine the other knife is the same.

As you point out, the steel hones/steels are meant for realigning the blade's edge and aren't meant to grind/sharpen.

Sharpening steels are either diamond coated or ceramic and either type will grind a steel blade's edge. The levels on the sharpening devices is grit/mesh, with lower numbers being more aggressive at removing steel.
